body:
Relevant to the License Inclusion Principles:

This appears to be a variety of "source available" license and (despite the issue submitter's statement to the contrary) is not a "free, open source license" as understood in the SPDX community and as traditionally understood in the FOSS community.

Also, while the issue submitter has said that "several complex, socially impactful projects utilize this license", it is fairly clear that the listed projects are a set of a few recently launched personal projects by the submitter that seem not to have any significant use at this time.

Finally, the issue submitter says that they have submitted the license for OSI approval, but this appears to be a false statement.

> Relevant to the License Inclusion Principles:
> 
> This appears to be a variety of "source available" license and (despite the issue submitter's statement to the contrary) is not a "free, open source license" as understood in the SPDX community and as traditionally understood in the FOSS community.
> 
> Also, while the issue submitter has said that "several complex, socially impactful projects utilize this license", it is fairly clear that the listed projects are a set of a few recently launched personal projects by the submitter that seem not to have any significant use at this time.
> 
> Finally, the issue submitter says that they have submitted the license for OSI approval, but this appears to be a false statement.

I would like to sincerely apologize for the erroneous submission. Indeed, the license I proposed does not meet the criteria for a FOSS license according to the traditional definition of the SPDX/OSI community.

My intention was to contribute based on experiences from social and educational projects I developed for the Brazilian Industrial Innovation and Robotics Olympiad. These projects are recent and have historical social impact, but I understand that this does not justify the misuse of terminology.

I also acknowledge the error regarding the OSI submission claim—it was an oversight on my part, and I thank you for pointing it out. I reiterate my respect for the FOSS community and its principles. I am reviewing everything with greater responsibility.
